transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Liam O'Connor: Hey Maya, Liam here. Priya and Sara with me as well.
[00:09] Priya Desai: Hi all, Priya.
[00:11] Sara Kim: Sara here.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great. We planned 45 minutes but we had a few extra so we put 52 in the invite, hope that's okay.
[00:22] Evelyn Park: We'll keep it focused, main goals: review usage/cost, reliability notes, and next steps on Dedicated evaluation.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good — we've seen a bump in usage after the new inference pipeline rolled out, so wanted to understand cost impact and tail latencies.

[00:40] Rajat Singh: Quick data point from our side: NovaPulse is up ~28% M/M on token usage and the 95/99th tail latency has crept up for the long-form route. We pulled a basic profile earlier. I'll share more detailed traces.
[00:53] Priya Desai: Right, the long-form generation has long sequences and the KV cache isn't as effective — that was our suspicion.
[01:02] Maya Chen: Yep, that matches what we saw. Two levers: batching + prefix caching to reduce unit cost and dedicated capacity to stabilize tail latencies. Are you currently on the hosted plan?
[01:11] Liam O'Connor: Yes hosted today, small commit. We're exploring Dedicated because we need predictable SLOs for customer-facing features in Q4.
[01:20] Sara Kim: Also want to double-check legal/compliance: Do we have audit log retention and KMS integration for customer data?

[01:28] Evelyn Park: We do. I'll send SOC 2 + audit log guide and the KMS/HSM integration docs after this call. Quick note: for Private deployments we support VPC peering and on-prem packages if you need air-gapped, but that's a heavier lift.
[01:44] Priya Desai: For now VPC is fine, but we might need on-prem later. Can you outline the difference in unit costs vs hosted?

[01:52] Maya Chen: Sure — short answer: Dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale because you get reserved GPU pools and can use aggressive batching and quantization. We'll send an updated pricing proposal that shows break-even points at your projected Q4 volumes.
[02:04] Liam O'Connor: What's the expected uplift in reliability? Our main concern is tail lat and warm KV cache behavior during bursts.

[02:12] Rajat Singh: From our benchmarks, moving to Dedicated and enabling persistent KV shards plus warmed-up caches can drop 99th percentile by 30–60% depending on workload. We'll need to run a profiling session with your real traffic to be precise.
[02:28] Maya Chen: We'll propose a pilot: 2-week Dedicated trial on a small reserved pool, run your main route through it, compare p50/p95/p99 and cost. Does that sound reasonable?
[02:38] Priya Desai: Yes, pilot sounds good. Timeline-wise we'd want results before mid-September to make capacity decisions for Q4.
[02:46] Sara Kim: Also curious about safety nets — if Dedicated hits saturation, is there automatic fallback to hosted models?

[02:53] Rajat Singh: We support smart routing and fallback policies — you can set a policy to failover to a compatible hosted variant to avoid hard failures, but there's some reconfiguration for model variants and token limits.
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: Okay good. On security: we need encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs — are those available in both Hosted and Dedicated?
[03:13] Evelyn Park: Yes. Hosted supports server-side encryption and audit logs; Dedicated and Private add customer-managed KMS and longer retention SLAs. I'll send a matrix showing feature parity.
[03:25] Priya Desai: Perfect. For the profiling, what do you need from our side?
[03:30] Rajat Singh: We'll need a sample of representative traffic (anonymized), example prompts, and a few peak window times. Ideally a one-hour replay of traffic around peak.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: We can do that. We'll work with Priya to extract a sanitized replay by Friday.
[03:46] Maya Chen: Thanks. On costs, I'll send a per-route cost breakdown and a model/quantization recommendation — we noticed you have a mix of long and short prompts, so mixed-precision could help.
[03:58] Sara Kim: Any quick wins we can do now to reduce spend without impacting quality?

[04:02] Rajat Singh: Reduce prefix repetition, enable KV cache TTL tuning, and consider a two-model strategy: smaller model for short queries, large model for long-form. We can suggest a rollout plan.
[04:14] Priya Desai: That two-model approach makes sense. We also want to keep an eye on quantization artifacts. If quality drops we need alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[04:23] Evelyn Park: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; we can enable thresholds and regression alerts. We'll include setup steps in the doc.
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: Great. One more thing — do you have support SLAs for incident response?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Our Dedicated and Private tiers include higher SLA options and a faster P1 response window; we'll include the SLA matrix in the follow-up.
[04:44] Sara Kim: Awesome. Anything on roadmap alignment we should be aware of?
[04:48] Rajat Singh: We have an upcoming release focusing on improved KV shard warming and reduced context-switch cost for long sequences — should help your workloads, targeting late Sept rollout.
[04:58] Priya Desai: If that's late Sept, it lines up with our Q4 prep — good timing.
[05:02] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: we'll send usage/cost breakdown, SOC 2 + KMS docs, schedule profiling deep-dive, and provide a Dedicated pricing proposal. Any objections?
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: No objections. Thanks everyone.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and the pilot proposal. Bye all.
[05:20] (call ends)
